startup.name: Lucis
startup.description: Lucis is a consumer preventive health service for Europe, described as Function Health for Europe. Members get regular blood testing combined with medical review and AI to turn results into actions for a longer healthy life. Members pay a subscription. Team of 17 in Paris, Spring 2025 batch. Traction, price and member counts are unknown.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the Spring 2025 batch, so this is a note only. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. A seventeen person team, an existing product category with a proven US model and a clear paying consumer would lift a cold application well above that, while a European consumer health service with regulated lab partners is a harder fit.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because a copy of a US company for another region is judged on execution and speed, and consumer health subscription retention is hard. Reviewers would also ask how a 17 person team funds lab costs and clinicians, and why blood tests are not a commodity that retailers already sell.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed fails if member growth is paid by ads with weak retention, since blood testing is bought once or twice a year and lab and clinician costs sit on every member. European seed funds put smaller amounts into consumer health, and SiPhox Health and Mito Health show that the rounds that got done were tied to hardware or a lean at cost model. Instalab and Mederva grew without a disclosed round.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 19 months needs thousands of retained members and unit economics that survive lab and clinician cost. Consumer testing companies in the data rarely get to an A quickly: SiPhox Health reached one after raising a seed and building hardware, and Mederva and Instalab have not shown one. Investors also compare to Function Health scale in the United States.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C requires a pan European health platform with insurer or employer channels and sustained profitability on testing. The data show few consumer preventive health companies reaching this stage, and Europe fragments the market by language, lab regulation and reimbursement, so the path to scale is long and uncertain.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in a stall or a small acquisition. Consumer testing companies in the data either stayed small, such as Instalab and Mederva, or were absorbed, as Eat Blueprint was by Blueprint. A full miss follows if member retention is low or if lab partners and retailers sell comparable panels cheaper.

killers.risk: Weak retention because testing is episodic
killers.evidence: Members need results only a few times a year, and Instalab and Mederva show growth without a venture round.
killers.mitigation: Add continuous touchpoints, such as coaching and prescriptions, and report 12 month retention.

killers.risk: Cheaper commodity blood tests from retailers and labs
killers.evidence: Thriva sells subscription blood tests and Healf sells at home tests from £79.
killers.mitigation: Win on interpretation and clinician follow up, not the draw.

killers.risk: Regulatory and lab differences across European countries
killers.evidence: Public insurance does not cover elective preventive blood testing, and lab rules differ by country.
killers.mitigation: Launch in two markets with certified lab partners before expanding.

killers.risk: Investor skepticism of a regional copy
killers.evidence: A region copy is judged on speed, and funded US leaders may enter Europe.
killers.mitigation: Build local clinical partnerships and data in languages the US firms lack.

technical_complexity.rationale: The product relies on lab partners and clinicians, so the build is a member app, ordering and result interpretation on top of existing labs. A small team can ship that in three months. The hard parts are clinical quality, consent and data protection under European law, and lab logistics, not software.

takeover_risk.rationale: A US leader could enter Europe and local players can add longevity panels, but cross border lab logistics and language slow rivals. A funded rival needs about a year.

evidence.claim: European consumers can already buy subscription blood tests and longevity panels from several companies, so some paid demand exists.
Preventive blood testing is fragmented and often not covered by public insurance, which pushes it to a paid consumer market.

actions: Reach several thousand paying members with 12 month retention data.
Publish outcomes such as biomarker improvement or follow up testing rates.

Short, easy to say in many European languages

narrative.headline: A well staffed European copy of a proven US model, with just under even odds of a seed inside 19 months.
narrative.general_summary: Lucis sells blood testing and AI interpretation to European consumers. Consumers already buy subscription tests in Europe and the 17 person team can build quickly, but retention is the open question and cheaper panels exist. The seed estimate for the 19 month window sits just under the consumer and healthcare anchors after discounting for the window, and does not rank this company against others. The funded analog in the data, SiPhox Health, had a hardware edge, and the lean ones raised small rounds. A Series A inside the window is unlikely.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2025-04-07, using the description file and market searches only.
Window is 19.3 months. Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors closing inside the window; series_a given seed is for the same window.
Consumer and Healthcare 2022-2025 cohorts are small (16 and 22 companies), so rates are anecdotes.
Several market search results named the company itself or were dated after the as of date; they were ignored (LEAK-WEB: lucis).
Price, member counts and retention are unknown.
